title: Discovery hub routing policy & telemetry workspace
content:
Purpose:
This is a working workspace for a lightweight "Discovery Hub" concept: a federated control-plane component that centralizes service discovery decisions and node capability indexing across regions. Aim is to simplify routing policy enforcement, surface GPU compatibility, and provide a compact health signal index that downstream routers can query quickly.

Background / motivation:
- We currently have multiple discovery layers: local kube service registry, per-region inventory caches, and ad-hoc routing logic in the edge proxy. This duplication leads to stale capability info and makes multi-region failover brittle.
- Many routing failures trace back to subtle GPU incompatibilities (driver mismatch, cuda patch level) or transient degraded nodes that are still 'Ready' but failing fast-path kernels.
- A small, consistent aggregated view (fingerprint + capability + health score) per node will let routing policies make better choices without expensive real-time probes.

Goals:
1) Define a compact per-node index (fingerprint) that captures immutable attributes + dynamic capability tags.
2) Provide a protocol for pushing health signals and scheduled heartbeat reconciliation.
3) Allow routing policy authors to express multi-criteria rules: region affinity, GPU feature filter, health threshold, cost tiering, drift tolerance.
4) Keep the Discovery Hub lightweight and eventually shoppable as a library for Private deployments.

Design sketch - Discovery Hub responsibilities:
- Ingest: node heartbeats, GPU profiler outputs, node metadata, and patch-level telemetry from the agent.
- Normalize: map raw GPU identifiers to canonical types and feature sets (e.g., quantization-friendly, bf16, fp16, sparse-support).
- Score: compute a rolling health score (0-100) combining heartbeat latency, recent kernel failures, eviction counts, and temperature throttling alerts.
- Expose: a small HTTP/gRPC index API for selectors and a push subscription model for routers to receive delta updates.
- Audit/log: append-only stream (compact) for reconciliation and drift detection.

Node identity and label model (proposal):
- fingerprint_id: sha1(node_uuid + region + gpu_serial) - stable until hardware swap.
- immutable_labels (set once at registration): region, zone, cpu_arch, machine_type, base_image, node_pool
- capability_tags (updated by agent): gpu_family (e.g., a100, h100), cuda_version, cudnn_version, quant_support=[int8,int4,bf16], fp16_fast_path, sparse_kernels
- runtime_tolerations: workloads can declare tolerations (e.g., tolerate-high-latency-cache, tolerate-throttling)

GPU taxonomy mapping (why we need it):
- Agents will report vendor strings and driver IDs. The Hub maintains a small mapping table -> canonical GPU features. This lets routing policies avoid brittle string compares and reason in capability predicates.
- Example canonical tags: "A100-80GB.PCIe", "H100-SXM.80GB", "A10G.24GB". Feature flags attached: [bf16, fp16-opt, int8-sparse, nvlink-topo].

Health signals and scoring (proposal):
- Signals consumed: heartbeat_ms, kernel_error_rate_5m, p95_token_latency_delta, thermal_throttle_events_1h, eviction_count_24h, disk_pressure_5m
- Scoring: weighted score: 40% kernel_error, 25% heartbeat freshness, 15% thermal, 10% eviction_history, 10% other. Scores normalized to 0-100 and stored as a short history (last 6 buckets).
- States derived: healthy (>85), degraded (60-85), warning (35-60), critical (<35).

Routing policy DSL (examples):
- Basic selection: region=="us-west1" AND gpu_family=="H100" AND health_state=="healthy"
- Cost-aware fallback: prefer region==primary THEN region==secondary with health_state>=60; allow quantized model route if gpu_supports.int8==true
- Canary routing: route 10% to new kernel-enabled pool where kernel_error_rate_5m < 0.02 and score >=90

Control-plane interactions and data paths:
- Agents push to regional Hub ingress (gRPC unary with TTL). Regional Hubs do local normalization and persist in the region's compact store (RocksDB-like).
- Global Hub shards subscribe to regional delta streams to synthesize cross-region views for cross-region routing (on-demand materialization).
- Routers query local Hub for fast selector evaluation; if not found or stale, router may call global view with fallback policy.

Multi-region considerations:
- Consistency model: eventually consistent with vector clocks per-node; we must accept slight staleness for routing to prioritize availability. Heartbeat TTLs are region-aware (shorter for intra-region failover).
- Regional affinity: default policy favors local region where latency matters; explicit cross-region routing requires health thresholds + cost delta check.
- Data residency: private deployments can opt-out of global replication; Discovery Hub supports local-only mode with same schemas.

Telemetry schema (compact):
- node_id, ts_iso, fingerprint_id, health_score, health_state, top_errors (list of strings), gpu_tags (list), heartbeat_ms
- Telemetry payloads are intentionally narrow to keep delta sizes small (prefer lists of codes over verbose messages).

Operational runbooks (initial):
- On rising kernel_error_rate_5m: mark node degraded, evict new long-running requests, schedule kernel re-probing in 5m.
- On score<35: mark node as drain candidate, notify SRE team, trigger automatic cordon if eviction_count>3 in 24h.
- Reconciliation job: daily pass to compute fingerprint drift and reconcile any nodes with changing immutable labels (flag for manual review).

Storage / capacity notes:
- Compact store per region: expect ~10k nodes in peak -> each node's record ~1KB (fingerprint, tags, last 6 scores) => ~10MB per region + overhead. Small and cheap.
- Delta streaming: protobuf with compact ints; typical update rate ~1-5s per node under load (check sampling options).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Exact fingerprint algorithm (sha1 vs murmur). Security notes: avoid exposing hardware serials in public endpoints.
- We need a canonical GPU feature catalog. Who owns it? Suggest applied-ml + platform to co-maintain.
- Policy DSL surface: integrate with existing rollout DSL or create a small standalone matcher? (Linked JIRA-INF-482)
- Backpressure behavior: how do agents retry when Hub is down? Backoff policy needed.

Immediate next steps:
- Prototype ingest endpoint + in-memory store (2 day spike) - implement sample agent to emit gpu tags. (Owner: Diego)
- Draft canonical GPU catalog and mapping tests (Owner: Priya)
- Sketch router query API and sample selector eval (Owner: Ava)

References:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Discovery+Hub+Overview
- Related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789
- Slack thread: #infra-discovery (see pinned messages)

Notes to self:
- Keep the Hub intentionally minimal. Biggest win is a deterministic, small index that router teams can depend on.
- Expect iterations: start with health_score + basic tags and add features only when needed.
